reference.source: WHO Classification of Tumours of the CNS
clinicalPearls: A highly aggressive embryonal tumour of infancy and early childhood, most often occurring under three years of age
Defined by biallelic inactivation of SMARCB1 (INI1) or, rarely, SMARCA4, a component of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodelling complex
May arise in the posterior fossa or supratentorially and frequently disseminates through the cerebrospinal fluid at diagnosis
Histology shows rhabdoid cells alongside primitive embryonal, mesenchymal and epithelial elements, mimicking other embryonal tumours
Loss of nuclear INI1 (SMARCB1) staining on immunohistochemistry is the diagnostic hallmark and distinguishes it from medulloblastoma
Molecular studies define subgroups (ATRT-TYR, ATRT-SHH, ATRT-MYC) with differing age and location patterns
Some cases reflect a germline SMARCB1 mutation (rhabdoid tumour predisposition syndrome), warranting genetic counselling
reference.pathophysiology: Atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumour is driven by inactivation of the SWI/SNF chromatin-remodelling complex, most commonly through loss of the SMARCB1 (INI1) tumour-suppressor gene and, in a minority, SMARCA4. Loss of this complex disrupts control of gene transcription and cellular differentiation, producing a poorly differentiated, rapidly proliferating tumour with characteristic rhabdoid cytology. The genome is otherwise relatively stable, with the SMARCB1/SMARCA4 loss being the central oncogenic event. Distinct epigenetic subgroups arise depending on the transcriptional programmes that become dysregulated, and a proportion of children harbour a germline predisposing mutation.
additionalDifferentials: Extrarenal malignant rhabdoid tumour with CNS involvement
additionalInvestigations: Contrast-enhanced brain MRI to define the mass and its location
Craniospinal MRI to evaluate for leptomeningeal dissemination
CSF cytology for staging once safe to obtain
Histopathology with INI1 (SMARCB1) and SMARCA4 immunohistochemistry
Molecular/methylation profiling to confirm diagnosis and subgroup
Germline SMARCB1/SMARCA4 testing and screening for extracranial rhabdoid tumours
redFlags: Very young infant with a rapidly enlarging intracranial mass and obstructive hydrocephalus
Evidence of CSF dissemination at presentation
Rapid neurological deterioration reflecting aggressive growth
Family history suggesting rhabdoid tumour predisposition syndrome
reference.prognosis: Historically one of the most aggressive paediatric brain tumours with a poor prognosis, particularly in infants and those with metastatic disease. Intensified multimodal regimens combining surgery, chemotherapy and, where age permits, radiotherapy have improved outcomes for some children, but survival remains limited, especially where radiotherapy must be withheld because of very young age.
pitfalls: Misclassifying the tumour as medulloblastoma or another embryonal tumour without INI1/SMARCA4 immunostaining
Failing to test for a germline SMARCB1 mutation and to offer family counselling and surveillance
Overlooking synchronous extracranial rhabdoid tumours, particularly renal, in affected infants
Delaying staging investigations, leading to inadequate treatment planning
references: WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System
Louis DN et al. The 2021 WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System
management: Maximal safe surgical resection of the tumour as the initial mainstay
Intensive multimodal chemotherapy, frequently high-dose regimens with autologous stem-cell rescue
Focal or craniospinal radiotherapy where age permits, constrained in infants by neurotoxicity
Intrathecal chemotherapy and directed management of leptomeningeal dissemination
Supportive care: cerebrospinal fluid diversion for hydrocephalus, corticosteroids for peritumoural oedema, and antiemetic and nutritional support
Surveillance neuraxis MRI and cerebrospinal fluid cytology for recurrence
Germline SMARCB1/SMARCA4 testing, genetic counselling and screening for extracranial rhabdoid tumours
Paediatric neuro-oncology multidisciplinary care including neurosurgery, oncology and palliative support
